text:
Rickard Rakell spent the week as the most talked-about man in Pittsburgh for something he didn't do. TSN and others reported that his no-trade list blocked a deal to Chicago, and the RMNB headline on Thursday morning was about the Penguins "preparing for potential fire sale." So it fit that Rakell scored both Pittsburgh goals that night. It also fit that the St. Louis Blues won 5-2 anyway.

Pittsburgh had the better first period by a distance, 1.31 to 0.38 in expected goals (the quality of the chances each side created), and Rakell's tip-in, set up by Trevor van Riemsdyk and Kris Letang, made it 1-0. Then the second period flipped completely. Justin Barron tied it with a wrist shot our numbers gave a 2% chance, the least likely goal of the night, and the Blues piled up 2.47 expected goals in the period. Dylan Holloway tipped one in at 9:14, and Jimmy Snuggerud finished a Robert Thomas and Jake Neighbours setup at 17:20. Arturs Silovs did stop Pius Suter on a 40% look in between, the biggest save of the game.

Snuggerud scored again off the same two passers early in the third, and that line was the story for St. Louis: 2.54 expected goals for with Thomas on the ice against 0.84 against. Thomas finished with three assists, Snuggerud with two goals on four shots. He's been a popular waiver pickup in fantasy leagues this month, and nights like this are why.

Here's the twist. By the full count, Pittsburgh deserved this one 59% of the time (deserved to win is the share of replays of every shot a team would win), and the third period was even. The difference was Joel Hofer, who saved 2.07 goals more than his 33 shots deserved and added the most wins of anyone on the ice. Rakell's second goal, a 74% chance set up by Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin, got through late, and Holloway's second goal at 17:16 made it 5-2.

For the Penguins, the result lands on top of a week of trade talk around Erik Karlsson, Malkin and Letang. Losing a game you out-chanced for long stretches won't change that conversation.
headline: Rakell stays, scores twice, and the Blues still roll
